source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.habit: Fast-growing tree to 20 m, root-sprouting colonies, brittle branches
morphology_documented.leaves: Alternate pinnate leaves with up to 27 leaflets, unpleasant smell, otherwise entire leaflets with basal teeth and glands
morphology_documented.flowers: Many small yellow-green flowers in terminal panicles, mainly unisexual, male flowers strong-smelling
morphology_documented.fruit: Twisted one-seeded winged mericarps 3–5 cm, 2–5 per fruit, red-tinted with age

source_scope_note: Historic taxonomic rank maintained; comparative key traits or family-only descriptions not automatically promoted to accepted species level.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Introduced from China; flora reports allelopathy and potential skin irritation, not native
preservation: Additive species source references only; no original records, photos, credits or galleries changed
